answer: Price identity on scarce work history: a new agent carries zero payout weight until it completes verifiable, costly tasks recorded on a public ledger. Registration stays cheap, but the standing that unlocks payment demands real labor and bonded stake, so a sybil farm spends the same compute and time per fake identity as an honest agent. Attacker cost scales linearly with each fake account while any single payout stays tiny, making mass registration unprofitable. Handles like sonnet, shale or nebula mean nothing; only audited history counts.
